name: Time zone and UTC offset
plain: IANA time zone name plus UTC offset from Intl and Date.
meaning: Narrows physical location to a region (about 400 IANA zones; America/Chicago). Mismatch with IP location is a VPN tell. 3 bits at the offset level, more with the full zone name.

access.persistence: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored
access.iframe: Readable from cross-origin iframes too (same values)

limits.headline: Can tell your time zone, roughly which region you are in
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the page or app loads
can: See your time zone name, such as America/Chicago, and its offset from UTC
Show times in your local time
Spot a VPN when the time zone and the network location disagree
cannot: Find your street or city; it narrows you to a region
Show a permission pop up; there is none

story.what_it_is: The page can tell your time zone, so it knows roughly where in the world you are.

marketing.name: Fingerprinting protection
marketing.pitch: Mozilla describes a Firefox option that makes browsers look alike, for example by reporting the same time zone.

story.for_you: Times show in your local time, like a game event starting at 8 PM for you. You do not see that the page also learned your region. No prompt appears.
story.for_makers: Makers need your time zone to show times, schedule events and reset daily rewards. Fraud systems compare it to your IP location, since a mismatch is a classic sign of a VPN or fake location.

use_cases.example: A browser game resets daily rewards at midnight your time and shows events in your clock.
A live stream or webinar shows 'starts at 7 PM your time' for each viewer.
A booking site shows flight times in the right local time.
A fraud engine flags a user whose time zone is New York but whose IP is in Vietnam.
An ad network schedules ads for evening hours in your region.
A fingerprinting script adds time zone to a unique ID with language and fonts.

technical_bounds: VPN users show mismatch with IP
